Each rule: id (kebab-case, unique), area, rule (what holds), source (the owner's words and date where known, the record it is kept in), enforced_by (kind ci-step: a step name in .github/workflows/*.yml or a check's `# check:` name in tools/checks/; world-rule: a rule id tools/checks/lib/world_rules.py fails under; absence: a numbered (N) block of the step 'Absences are enforced'; hook: a .claude/hooks file that cites the rule's id; permission-deny: an entry of .claude/settings.json's permissions.deny; prose: written down only, checked by people). CI ('The rules are data, and the hooks hold', tools/checks/lib/rules_check.py) proves every reference exists.

rules.rule: hour.js's one crypto.getRandomValues is the page's one entropy read: written whole as data-seed, it picks the visit's opening, one of a set (the hour's sky by 16 seeds: 96 openings; the seed is read mod 16), and seeds everything after the opening (the frame after the cut the world draws the sky order after the skies on show, the events, the ink birds' later flocks and the score from the read itself); what is on screen at the cut, the land among it, is the opening seed's. The world draws no entropy of its own. The world's one clock is clockNow() (performance.now), read for budgets only. The kits, wing model, ink birds, plan's worker and the sound icon's switch and score draw no entropy and read no clock of the page's (they time the sound by the audio context's own time, ctx.currentTime, which times the sound alone; the score's randomness is a stream on a seed the world derives from its one read and hands over, read only, in WORLD.sky). hour.js reads the clock once (new Date). No Math.random, no Date in the world.

rules.rule: No innerHTML and no JS-generated DOM: the canvas, the stack, the footer (the sound icon in it) and the lettered name are all in index.html; the sound icon plays its score through Web Audio, never an audio element (none is made, and none is in the page).

No URL hook (location., URLSearchParams), network call or eval, but one: no sound until the visitor presses the sound icon, and then sound.js alone makes the one audio context, inside that press, and fetches the one sheet of notes (a literal path under /assets/sound/, from 'self'), once, for the score (score.js) to play; the score makes no context and fetches nothing; nothing of it is fetched or made before. No worker but the plan's, started by its literal name; no module or audio worklet; no cursor: rule (OS cursors only). The site's own code is blind: no telemetry, beacon or store (Cloudflare Web Analytics, injected by Cloudflare, is the one exception).

rules.rule: The shipped scripts carry no development harness: no window.__*, window.claude or console call, and no attribute read on <html> but the hour's data-sky, data-sky-at and data-seed.

CSP is set per HTML path with no overlapping rules (Cloudflare Pages combines same-named headers, and browsers enforce the intersection); never a Content-Security-Policy on /*. 404.html carries the same policy in a meta tag, kept in sync. Every home-scope CSP has exactly script-src 'self' https://static.cloudflareinsights.com and connect-src https://cloudflareinsights.com https://derekzhou.com/cdn-cgi/rum, and the home page's (/ and /index.html) connect-src names 'self' first, for the sound icon's one sheet of notes (fetched only at the press; 2026-11-07); 404.html's does not. No inline style, script or handler on a CSP'd page.

The scripts load in their order (hour, site.js, the sound icon's switch, the world, the kits, the wing model, the ink birds, the sound icon's score), each tagged data-cfasync="false" for Rocket Loader; no script is async; the world, the kit and the realms are parser-blocking after the footer (the first-paint hold), the wing model, the ink birds and the score deferred; the head holds one link rel=expect href=#world-end blocking=render, and the body one empty, hidden <div id="world-end"> right after the last realm's script (the render block ends there).
Nothing but the site is served: site/ holds only the kinds of file the site serves, the root only the repository's own; CLAUDE.md, .github/ and the font scripts stay outside the build.
Nothing built is committed: a change is made in src/ and committed alone, and the build (tools/build.mjs) makes the rest, the same bytes every time.

Everything but HTML is cached immutable, so changed bytes need a new name: the build names scripts and the stylesheet by content; fonts and images are renamed by hand, with every reference, in the same commit.

Every visit of a device compiles the same shader sources, and every program compiles; which programs a change edits is the gate's census of the base's and the head's builds, never a committed file (a returning visitor's shader cache depends on it).

The page says exactly its words: the lettered name, the one line, the credit row (Team Lead · Accenture Song · 2022 – Now), the two links and the sound icon, whose accessible name is Sound (a button, its state in aria-pressed; no visible word); the share and search text match.

rules.rule: The sound is opt-in: every visit is silent until the visitor presses the sound icon (a button in the footer, in the words' light ink, its state in aria-pressed, which is always the truth: a failed fetch or decode, or a device that will not start, shows it off). The press sets the audio session to playback (heard with the iOS ringer off, as a video is; the visitor's own music pauses), makes one audio context, fetches one sheet of notes from this site (/assets/sound/: real recordings, CC0) and decodes it once, and hands both to the score (score.js), which plays music and faint ambiance live, following the sky (each sky its key and its colour, its changes planned with the world's, never a loop), its level rising over about 4 s; a second press takes it down over about 1.5 s and suspends the context, a third resumes it. A visit that never presses loads the switch and the score's code (about 0.6 and 5.9 KB as sent, the score deferred) and no audio. The score sits at about -26 LUFS; it reads the sky (WORLD.sky, a copy) and never steers the world.
